notes.title: ViewTracker 1.03
notes.notes:
ViewTracker 1.03 changelog:
[list]
[*] Tracking improvements: more responsive and smooth. New filtering system specified as a percentage from 0-90%.
[*] Performance improvements:
  * maintain high tracking frame rates even while running demanding games
  * optionally makes use of multiple CPU cores
  * smoother tracking while initializing during first 1-2 minutes
[*] Camera settings: set a framerate and resolution for each camera. Defaults to 640x480 @ 30FPS
[*] Optional FPS counter
[*] Fixed a bug that could cause initial position to be off center
[/list]

ViewTracker 1.03 is here!! The performance improvements along with the more stable and responsive filtering combine to make tracking feel super smooth and natural.

Note to PS3 Eye users: an updated [url=https://github.com/jkevin/PS3EyeDirectShow/releases]PS3 Eye driver[/url] has been posted.

The new camera configuration options allow you to specify a framerate and resolution. The default of 640x480 at 30 frames per second (fps) should be a good tradeoff in most situations. Higher resolutions use more system resources, and if your face occupies a region larger than 125x125 pixels ViewTracker scales it down internally anyway. Most cameras only allow up to 30 fps, but some cameras (I'm looking at you, PS3 Eye) allow up to 60 fps. That's wonderful because in good lighting conditions that can make for very responsive tracking, but higher frame rates do come with some tradeoffs. A higher frame rate means the camera has less time per frame to collect light, and this means noise levels will be higher. This makes for less accurate tracking that will require more smoothing. Another thing to keep in mind is ViewTracker uses a lot of CPU power per frame in order to make accurate predictions. It would be possible to reduce the accuracy and use less CPU power (therefor allowing a higher frame rate), but this would again just require more smoothing and defeat the purpose of having a higher frame rate to begin with. In order to have good accuracy at 60 fps, ViewTracker now makes use of up to 4 CPU cores. This can have a larger performance impact on your game, especially if your CPU has 4 cores or less. So long story short, I have found the better tradeoff is often to track at 30 fps. That said, if you have bright lighting and a powerful CPU, tracking at 60 fps is prettay nice.

notes.title: PS3 Eye Camera Open Source Driver (32 / 64 bit)
notes.notes:
I have been working on a driver for the PlayStation Eye Camera and [url=https://github.com/jkevin/PS3EyeDirectShow/releases]the first beta release is now available on github[/url]! Happily there were lots of open source projects out there that were of great help, including the PS3 Eye Linux driver.

For those who are unfamiliar with this camera, it's an extremely good value (only $7 on Amazon right now) and it has a decent sensor which is capable of 60 FPS at a low latency. It's perfect for head tracking, but the only problem is it's designed to be used with a PlayStation 3. There is another 3rd party driver available for PC but it's only for 32 bit apps and doesn't work with ViewTracker.

The new driver has only had limited testing and could still have some bugs. The good news is that it runs in user-mode so any bugs will only affect the app that's using the camera and it won't crash your entire computer like a kernel-mode driver could. It should be compatible with any DirectShow application. If you run into any issues please feel free to post feedback here or on github.

Hope everyone is having fantastic holiday season!

notes.title: ViewTracker 1.02
notes.notes:
ViewTracker 1.02 has been released and includes the following fixes:

- Fixed an issue preventing users with a private Steam profile from accessing the demo
- Added error message when unable to open the camera
- Stability improvements

notes.title: Demo!
notes.notes: Now you can download a free 7 day trial of ViewTracker! Just click the download demo button on the right side of the page. If you're not sure how well head tracking will work for you or you don't know whether ViewTracker will work with your particular camera and lighting conditions this is the perfect way to try it out. Please note that your Steam profile must be at least level one for the demo to work. The demo will expire 7 days after your first tracking session. Enjoy!

notes.title: ViewTracker 1.01 Update Released
notes.notes:
ViewTracker 1.01 is out with several fixes and some new features:

- Fixed problem restarting app after a crash
- Stability improvements
- Fixed issue where some webcams would run at less than 30 fps
- Minor performance improvements
- Support for Prepar3d v4 via SimConnect
- vjoystick support (requires installing vjoystick driver)
- Option to hide green box around face in video preview

Thank you to everyone who has tried out ViewTracker so far! Please feel free to let me know how it's working or any changes you would like to see.

notes.title: Working through some launch issues
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

Thanks so much to everyone that has posted feedback so far. I have just made a quick update to fix an issue with Arma III and probably some other games as well. I'll work on getting other issues fixed as fast as possible. I'm also working on a guide to explain configuration options for some games. I'll try to update it with as many games as I can over time. Thank you for trying out ViewTracker and thanks for your patience while these issues get sorted out.

notes.title: ViewTracker has been released!
notes.notes:
I'm super excited to introduce ViewTracker — a new solution for head tracking on PC! As a PC gamer that very much enjoys a good simulation, I know how much head tracking can improve the gaming experience. There are a lot of head tracking solutions out there, but I feel like there's a need for something that's simple and inexpensive that will make it easy for more people to experience how awesome it is to game with head tracking. The only hardware that's required is a webcam. There's plenty of futuristic machine learning techie stuff going on under the hood to make that possible but for the end user it should be as easy as plugging in a webcam and pressing a button.

I've put in a lot of work into getting tracking to work well with only a webcam and I couldn't be happier to be bringing it out on Steam. Huge thanks to the opentrack project for making their work available under a permissive license. This allowed me to bring out ViewTracker without having to reinvent the wheel but instead make use of a tried and true user interface. Happy simming!
